certification.name: PyTorch Core: Practical ML & Neural Networks

concepts.name: Dataset and DataLoader roles
concepts.description: `Dataset` stores or retrieves samples and labels, while `DataLoader` wraps a dataset with iteration, batching, sampling, and optional multiprocessing.

concepts.name: Custom Dataset methods
concepts.description: A map-style custom `Dataset` typically implements `__len__` for dataset size and `__getitem__` for retrieving one indexed sample.

concepts.name: DataLoader batching and shuffle
concepts.description: `DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=..., shuffle=...)` can automatically form minibatches and optionally reshuffle map-style data between epochs.

concepts.name: Iterating minibatches
concepts.description: Iterating a `DataLoader` yields batches whose structure is produced by dataset samples and the collate step.

concepts.name: DataLoader workers
concepts.description: `num_workers` controls how many subprocesses a `DataLoader` uses for data loading, with 0 meaning loading occurs in the main process.

concepts.name: Pinned memory and non-blocking transfer
concepts.description: `pin_memory=True` asks DataLoader to return tensors in pinned host memory, which can improve CPU-to-CUDA transfer performance.

concepts.name: Custom collation
concepts.description: `collate_fn` controls how a list of individual dataset samples is merged into a batch.

concepts.name: Transforms
concepts.description: Transforms preprocess samples or targets before they are consumed by the model.

questions.explanation: Dataset stores or retrieves samples and labels, while DataLoader wraps a dataset with iteration, batching, sampling, and optional multiprocessing. Use a DataLoader to iterate through minibatches instead of manually slicing the full dataset in the training loop. A Dataset and a DataLoader solve different problems: one defines samples and the other defines how samples are delivered.
hints: Use a DataLoader to iterate through minibatches instead of manually slicing the full dataset in the training loop.

questions.explanation: num_workers controls how many subprocesses a DataLoader uses for data loading, with 0 meaning loading occurs in the main process. Increase num_workers when data preparation is a measured input bottleneck, then profile because the best value depends on workload and platform. More workers are not automatically faster and can increase memory use or process overhead.
hints: Increase num_workers when data preparation is a measured input bottleneck, then profile because the best value depends on workload and platform.

questions.explanation: pin_memory=True asks DataLoader to return tensors in pinned host memory, which can improve CPU-to-CUDA transfer performance. A common CUDA pattern combines a pinned DataLoader with tensor.to(device, non_blocking=True). Pinned memory is primarily a host-to-accelerator transfer optimization, not a universal CPU speedup.
hints: A common CUDA pattern combines a pinned DataLoader with tensor.to(device, non_blocking=True).

A custom collate function changes batch construction; it does not replace the Dataset itself.
